category_feedback.specific_evidence: lesson_specific_materials lists 'Per-pair set of base-ten blocks including thousand-cubes' and 'Per-child place-value mat (Th, H, T, O columns)' as required, with no no-paper, no-purchase fallback path described in differentiation. Children who arrive on a no-prep day cannot run the lesson.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a NO-PAPER, NO-PURCHASE alternative path to differentiation: e.g., 'No-materials version — children use four fingers on a hand as Th/H/T/O columns, raise stand-up bodies for hundreds, kneel for tens, sit for ones; or use voice chant 9-hundreds-0-tens-5-ones for 905.' Make explicit that the lesson is runnable with body and voice alone.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Penny anchors minds_on and consolidation, all success_criteria start with 'I can', and vocabulary has child-friendly defs — but consolidation discussion_prompts and exit_routine end without a distinctive quotable refrain or memorable chant for children. exit_routine = 'Each child writes one number between 100 and 1000 on a sticky note plus its expanded form.'
category_feedback.required_fix: Give Penny a distinctive quotable refrain children chant back at the consolidation, e.g., 'Every digit has a PLACE — and every place has a VALUE!' Add it to teacher_script in minds_on and to exit_routine so children carry it across all five lessons. Consider a hand gesture (slap thigh on PLACE, point up on VALUE).

category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough names the zero-placeholder trap and gives concrete recovery (position-by-position read, build-before-read, phone-number analogy) but never names the underlying research framework. No invitation for children to invent or compare strategies — Stations A/B/C are all teacher-prescribed 'build it / match it' tasks.
category_feedback.required_fix: Cite Fuson's place-value sequence research or Ross's five levels of place-value understanding by name in expanded_walkthrough.rationale; and add a step in action where pairs invent two different ways to represent 1000 (one thousand-cube vs ten hundred-flats vs 100 ten-rods) and compare which build makes the structure clearest, before sharing strategies in consolidation.

summary: Math pair 1 has strong alignment (B1.1 + B1.5 cleanly addressed), a real research-grounded zero-placeholder trap with concrete branched recovery, and a worksheet that practises the lesson's success criteria with deliberate generalization (six zero-placeholder numbers in Part 2). Three lesson-side categories sit at 3: no no-paper alternative path, no quotable Penny refrain or memorable chant for children to carry forward, and no named research citation or invent-and-compare strategy moment. All blocking fixes are in lesson_01; the worksheet stands.
